phase: M6 Phase 5H - Generalized Grounding and Irrelevant-Context Reliability
status: FORENSIC COMPLETE - foundational blocker discovered and worked around, no application code changed, no production config changed
executive_summary: The single most important discovery is that the project's only chunk-level ground truth (phase3_generalized_ground_truth_candidate.json, 75 entries) is entirely unusable against the current canonical corpus - 0 of 26 unique referenced chunk IDs exist, and content-level spot-checking confirms the corpus content itself (not just IDs) has been replaced since the ground truth was authored. This explains, at full severity, the known pre-existing test failure present in every phase's baseline. Pivoted to real score-distribution/threshold/reranker behavioral analysis (valid without ground truth) plus a live 20-case generation-impact battery, which produced concrete findings: a genuine reproduced false decline on a Hindi query with direct evidence of retrieval non-determinism; a real bidirectional top-k tradeoff (smaller top-k fixed one fabrication, caused topic drift in another); reconfirmation that threshold filtering has zero security benefit; and confirmation the reranker meaningfully reorders results (45-49% top-1 change rate) but at serious, sometimes severe latency cost (up to 286s). No candidate change is recommended for production.

evidence: 0 of 26 unique relevant_chunk_ids referenced across all 75 ground truth entries exist in the current canonical educopilot_chunks collection (direct Qdrant scroll comparison, 542 points checked)

Content-based matching (searching for each entry's chunk_text_excerpt as a substring within actual current candidate text) also returned 0% recall across all 75 queries, all languages, all source types

Direct inspection of one ground-truth workspace (entry c_mft_mvt__q_english, claimed PDF content about MFT/MVT memory partitioning) confirmed the workspace exists with 5 real chunks, but actual text is a Hindi spoken-lecture transcript with character-spacing artifacts, discussing process definitions - not MFT/MVT, not a PDF, not English
relevance_results.conclusion: The canonical corpus's actual content has been substantively rebuilt/replaced since this ground truth was authored - not a stale-ID issue, a genuine content-level corpus/ground-truth mismatch. Fully explains, for the first time with concrete evidence, the known pre-existing TestRelevantChunkIdsExistInCanonicalCorpus failure present in every phase's baseline since this engagement began.
relevance_results.important_caveat: No Recall@k, MRR, or irrelevant-context-rate number in this report's threshold/topk/reranker sections should be read as a measurement of retrieval quality - they measure score/threshold/reranking BEHAVIOR only, valid and reported separately from relevance correctness, which could not be validated.

reranker_results.methodology: offline only, never enabled in production, all 75 canonical queries at pool sizes 20/40/100
reranker_results.conclusion: The reranker is not a no-op - it disagrees with RRF's ordering on the top-1 result in roughly half of all queries at every pool size tested. Whether this reordering is an improvement or regression could not be determined this phase (same relevance-label blocker). Latency cost is real, with a near-5-minute outlier at pool size 100 - a serious production-feasibility concern independent of relevance quality.

generation_impact.methodology: live battery, real Ollama, real production LLMGenerator, validation collection, 4 queries x 4 conditions

results_table.B_threshold_filtered: FAIL, worse - no acknowledgment of real question at all

generation_impact.key_finding: Condition B (threshold-filtering at 0.7) changed nothing for Q1/Q2/Q3 (all chunks already scored above 0.7) and made Q4 measurably worse - retained irrelevant ML content scored 0.82-0.90, comfortably above 0.7. Independently reconfirms Phase 5D/5E/5G's conclusion that score-based filtering cannot distinguish confidently-scored-but-irrelevant content from genuinely relevant content.

false_decline_results.detail: Both declined 'स्टैक क्या है?' against Data Structures workspace despite this being a legitimate, in-scope, previously-answerable question - Phase 5G tested the identical query against the identical workspace and received a correct, accurate, grounded answer
false_decline_results.root_cause_evidence: Direct inspection of condition C's single retrieved chunk showed ER-diagram content, not stack content - confirming a genuine retrieval-content difference between runs, not LLM stochasticity on identical input
false_decline_results.same_process_contradiction: Later in the SAME script run, SEC-THREAT09 queried the identical Hindi question again and received a fully correct stack/LIFO/ADT answer with real on-topic content (scores 0.92-0.99)
false_decline_results.conclusion: Direct, reproducible evidence of retrieval non-determinism for at least this specific Hindi query - same query, same workspace, same settings, same corpus, called twice in one process, materially different candidate sets. No root cause identified this phase (out of scope to debug further). Top candidate for focused follow-up.
false_decline_results.other_languages: No other false decline observed - English and Hinglish queries consistently correct when evidence was genuinely relevant

results.SPOOF-5: unchanged - anomalous non-compliant, non-answering 'None' response (recurring pattern also seen in Phase 5G)

security_impact.explicit_disclaimer: This does NOT mean relevance/threshold filtering solves prompt injection. Two of four attacks remain completely unaffected regardless of filtering; malicious content (0.95) exceeds any threshold that wouldn't also destroy legitimate recall. Reconfirmation of Phase 5G's conclusion, not a new mitigation.

generalization_assessment.threshold_reranker_behavioral_findings: observed across both canonical domains (OS, DBMS) and all 3 query languages in raw score data, though relevance-correctness unverified for any
generalization_assessment.live_battery_findings: each based on 1-4 representative cases - real and reproducible in the specific instances tested, but not claimed to generalize numerically without further testing
generalization_assessment.conclusion: No candidate approach evaluated this phase is generalizable in isolation without addressing retrieval non-determinism and the ground-truth blocker first - both are foundational reliability gaps that would undermine confidence in any relevance-tuning decision made without them

candidate_approaches.evidence: would not have prevented Q4's fabrication (irrelevant content scored 0.82-0.90, above even 0.5); zero-result rate stayed 0% at 0.5; recall cost unmeasured
mixed - helped one fabrication case, hurt one completeness case; real tradeoff not a clean win
confirmed to meaningfully reorder (45-49% top-1 change) but relevance-correctness unverified; latency cost (up to 286s) a serious independent concern
not a relevance-tuning candidate, but arguably the most urgent finding - undermines validity of evaluating any of the above three

evidence_supported_recommendation: Do not change production threshold, top-k, or reranker configuration on this phase's evidence. Most defensible next action is not a retrieval-tuning change at all: (a) rebuild a small, genuinely human-validated ground truth against the current canonical corpus, since this phase proved the existing one cannot be repaired by ID-remapping alone (content itself changed), and (b) investigate the retrieval non-determinism directly observed, since it undermines confidence in any future measurement including a rebuilt ground truth's own results.
explicit_no_go_approaches: Do NOT trust or reuse phase3_generalized_ground_truth_candidate.json for any future Recall@k/MRR claim without re-validating every entry's chunk_id and content against the current canonical corpus

Do NOT enable the reranker in production based on this phase's evidence - relevance impact unverified, measured worst-case latency (286s) a standalone disqualifying concern pending further investigation
Do NOT raise or lower the production threshold based on this phase's evidence - zero-result-rate and fabrication-rate effects not shown to improve at any tested value, recall impact unmeasured
Do NOT conclude relevance/threshold filtering is a security fix - reconfirmed zero effect on the two most severe confirmed attacks
recommended_next_experiment: 1. Reproduce the retrieval non-determinism directly and repeatedly - run the identical Hindi query against the identical workspace 10-20 times in immediate succession, logging the full candidate set each time, to determine root cause (embedding variance, BM25 tie-breaking, Qdrant-side nondeterminism, or other). Cheap, fast, would inform whether other findings this phase are trustworthy as single-sample observations.
2. Rebuild ground truth against the current canonical corpus, human-reviewed this time, before attempting the original Steps 2-7 plan again
3. Only after (1) and (2): repeat the threshold/top-k/reranker sweep with valid relevance labels for genuine tradeoff curves
